comment: What the game draws and plays for each thing the simulation has: game IDs on the left, the asset pipeline's stable semantic IDs on the right.
Presentation data, not game content: nothing here changes a rule, a save or the content hash. An asset that is missing or will not load
falls back to its greybox. Every model is drawn at its authored size (the asset's semantic size is authoritative; nothing rescales
one to a collision shape): centred on its structure, its long side along the structure's, stood on the ground. Where the authored
size and the world's structure disagree by more than half a metre a side (or 0.6 m of height) the greybox stands and the mismatch
is reported. 'tile' repeats a modular piece (a fence panel) at its own length. Static models are the full files: every _lod1-3 file
in the library (1,455) carries no material. Weapons are held by their own SOCK_grip_primary. Sources: assets/manifests/
playable_prototype_assets.json (the player, the weapons, the den chest), phase1_environment.json, ashen_hollow_landmarks.json,

tree_.note: The procedural species (oak, pine, dead: _procgen_tree.py) at their authored 12.8-13.7 m, trunk vertical from the ground.

longhouse_.note: Drawn whole over its walls' footprint (the procedural lodge, built to these walls); the walls and roof stay the camera's colliders. Arrows striking it read as wood.

forge_.note: Drawn whole the same way (the procedural smithy, chimney over the hearth).
